title: MAHARASHTRA CLASS 3 — English | Conjunctions
description: Subject-wise test on Conjunctions (English) for MAHARASHTRA CLASS 3. 40Q.
subject: maha3-english

questions.question: Rohan likes to play cricket ______ football.
questions.explanation: 'And' is used to join two similar ideas or things. Rohan likes both cricket and football.
questions.subject: maha3-english

questions.question: My cat is small ______ it is very playful.
questions.explanation: 'But' is used to show a contrast. The cat is small, which might suggest it's quiet, but it is actually playful, showing a contrast.
questions.subject: maha3-english

questions.question: Do you want an apple ______ a banana for your snack?
questions.explanation: 'Or' is used to show a choice between two or more options. The question asks the child to choose between an apple and a banana.
questions.subject: maha3-english

questions.question: I am happy ______ it is my birthday today.
questions.explanation: 'Because' is used to give a reason. The reason for being happy is that it is the speaker's birthday.
questions.subject: maha3-english

questions.question: It was raining heavily, ______ I took my umbrella.
questions.explanation: 'So' is used to show the result or consequence of something. Taking the umbrella was a result of the heavy rain.
questions.subject: maha3-english

questions.question: My mother went to the market ______ bought some vegetables ______ fruits.
questions.explanation: 'And' is used to connect a sequence of actions or to list multiple items. She went to the market *and* then bought things. She bought vegetables *and* fruits.
questions.subject: maha3-english

questions.question: The sun was shining brightly, ______ it was still cold outside.
questions.explanation: 'But' is used to introduce a contrasting idea. Bright sunshine usually means warmth, but here it's still cold, showing a contrast.
questions.subject: maha3-english

questions.question: You must study hard ______ you will not pass the exam.
questions.explanation: 'Or' is used here to show a negative consequence if the first action (studying hard) is not performed. It implies "otherwise."
questions.subject: maha3-english

questions.question: Seema could not go out to play ______ she had to finish her homework.
questions.explanation: 'Because' provides the reason why Seema could not go out to play. The reason was her homework.
questions.subject: maha3-english

questions.question: My brother wanted to eat pizza, ______ I wanted pasta, ______ we decided to order both.
questions.explanation: 'But' shows the contrast in preferences (brother wanted pizza, I wanted pasta). 'So' indicates the result or decision made based on these differing preferences (we decided to order both).
questions.subject: maha3-english

options.text: The boy was tired, but he went to bed early.
The boy was tired, or he went to bed early.
The boy was tired, so he went to bed early.
The boy was tired, and he went to bed early.

questions.explanation: 'so' correctly shows that going to bed early was a result of being tired.

questions.question: Read the sentence: "You must study hard, ______ you will not pass the exam." Which conjunction best completes the sentence to show a consequence if the first action is not taken?

questions.question:
Look at the two sentences:
Sentence 1: The boy was hungry.
Sentence 2: He ate all his lunch.
Which conjunction correctly joins these two sentences to show a cause and its effect?

options.text: The boy was hungry *but* he ate all his lunch.
The boy was hungry *or* he ate all his lunch.
The boy was hungry, *so* he ate all his lunch.
The boy was hungry *and* he ate all his lunch.

questions.explanation: 'So' is the correct conjunction to show a cause-and-effect relationship. Being hungry was the cause, and eating all his lunch was the effect or result. Option A implies contrast, B implies choice, and D simply joins without a strong cause-effect link.
questions.subject: maha3-english
